update.reference: Key priorities of the future state
update.quote:
End-to-End Process Automation with Minimal Manual Intervention

- Automated, AI-powered data pipelines—from acquisition to dissemination— reduce manual effort, increase speed and quality, and enable real-time responsiveness across all stages of the statistical business process.

- Employee input focuses on higher value work, innovation, and interpretation, not execution.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicit reference to automation and AI-powered pipelines from acquisition to dissemination implicates every GSBPM phase and sub-phase, as the text highlights end-to-end process impact.

update.reference: Key priorities of the future state
update.quote:
Surveys as a last resort, not first response

- Exploiting existing data holdings is the first response for new/existing data needs. Admin data and alternative data is the second response for new/existing data needs. Surveys are only used if necessary and are optimized dynamically based on cost-benefit

- Designing, rendering and fielding a questionnaire is done using AI and takes no more than X time

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Using existing data sources and administrative/alternative data before resorting to surveys impacts needs specification, data availability checks, collection design, and survey sample design.
AI-driven questionnaire design and dynamic optimization impacts the tools for collection, affecting collection instrument design and implementation.
Survey minimization and dynamic fielding impacts how samples are selected and frames are created.

update.reference: Key priorities of the future state
update.quote:
Searchable, Usable, Actionable Data Assets

- All data and metadata are standardized, richly described, and machine-actionable—built for interoperability and reuse across tools, systems, and organizations.

- Discovery, understanding, and use are seamless for all types of users—whether human or machine—through APIs, metadata tagging, and open formats.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Standardization spans from data design through processing, analysis, and especially dissemination to guarantee machine-actionable and interoperable assets.
Standardized metadata and discoverability concerns are fundamental in dissemination steps and post-processing.

update.quote:
Expanded Digital Dissemination: Shift focus from static web publishing to dynamic, interactive, and API-driven platforms for more accessible and real-time data engagement.

Automation of Core Processes: Automate production and dissemination of data products (including data tables and PUMFs), improving speed, accuracy, and resource efficiency.

Metadata-First Approach: Implement comprehensive metadata standards and tagging, enabling external tools like ChatGPT, Gemini, and other AI agents to accurately discover and extract relevant data.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Focus on dissemination platforms and standards directly implicates output systems and dissemination steps.
Automation of product production and dissemination implicates dissemination product creation and release.

update.quote: Make PUMFs mandatory, use automated methods for creation of PUMFs

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Mandatory, automated production of microdata products affects how dissemination products are prepared for public use.

update.quote:
Discuss the type of product to disseminate before it gets to the end of the GSBPM process.

Not all projects require a data visualization for example as users will do it themselves.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Early discussion of dissemination products and need for data visualization ties dissemination design back to initial needs assessment and output definition.

update.quote: Incorporate AI agents capable of interpreting data-sharing agreements, executing governance policies dynamically (e.g., privacy, retention, classification), and mediating context-aware access based on metadata, provenance, and purpose.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Governance overlays the entire statistical data lifecycle but specifically impacts data access, privacy, and compliance steps in process, analyze, and disseminate phases.

update.quote: Shift from active data collection to a passive model for collection

update.quote:
Ensure minimum metadata requirements are respected for every data collection/acquisition process
Use AI to enhance the extraction of structured data from unstructured sources
Ensure metadata to identify credible data sources to reduce mis/dis-information
Automate recurring data acquisitions with external partners
Use AI/ML to populate metadata repositories (fill gaps) and IM data tagging, at ingestion

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Each collection or acquisition process must meet minimum metadata and reliability requirements, implicating collection setup.
Automating acquisition and metadata enrichment at ingestion implicates run and finalize collection.
Ensuring credibility and comprehensive metadata also implicates finalise stages.

update.quote:
Expand use of SDMX throughout the data lifecycle process
Leverage .STAT tools for data processing & analysis
Amplify use of AI/ML to apply classification codes/standards
Prescribe the use of data management tools (Aria/Colectica)

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Explicitly targets processing, analysis and standardization, involves SDMX, classification, and data management tool usage.
Tool usage for processing and analysis involves design and analytical phases.

update.quote:
GSBPM 5 sub-processes are orchestrated in modular, event-driven frameworks that are automated and version-controlled by design. Analysts are no longer required to manually intervene, clean or manipulate files.

AI-enabled modules handle 50% of manual interventions for activities such as classification, edits and imputation for administrative and survey data.

Every processing pipeline is auditable, reproducible, and deployable across subject-matter domains. Meta-data driven and standardization are default by design.

Data processing turnaround time has reduced by 50% across survey programs through automation and orchestration.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Orchestration and automation of processing pipelines directly reference GSBPM 5 and all its sub-phases, especially classification, imputation, derivation, aggregation.

update.quote: Emphasis on the need for the right people to handle technical aspects and the importance of standardizing data formats.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: Standardizing data formats, while not explicitly referencing a single phase, affects design, processing, analysis and dissemination.
Uniform formats for downstream use impact processing functions.

update.quote:
Implement AI-supported pipelines for auto-generated descriptive and exploratory analysis including daily write-ups, dashboards, and standardized analytical products.

Build infrastructure and tooling that enable real-time analytical workflows with intelligent validation and anomaly detection.

implicated phases and subphases.justification: AI-support for auto-generating outputs and dashboards directly impacts the drafting and interpretation steps within Analyse.
Validation/anomaly detection targets output validation.
